A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching research questions, models, and retained experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original component-patching, knockout, representation-analysis, and fine-tuning experiments, including Tables 1–5 and appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds method comparisons, sentence-level interventions, multilingual reasoning, statistical analyses, and domain and bias evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 uses standard whole-activation path patching. v3 introduces subspace-intervened patching: contrastive activation differences and an SVD-based decomposition identify a translation-steering subspace, and interventions replace only its projection while preserving the orthogonal component (Section 4.1, Algorithms 1–2). The targeted fine-tuning strategy remains broadly unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds Swahili, Bengali, and Arabic analysis; MGSM mathematical reasoning; medical and legal translation using ELRC-Medical-V2 and M3T; CAMT cultural translation; and French/Spanish gender and formality evaluations. Original WMT sentence-translation coverage, including Russian, Japanese, and Czech directions, remains present.

E2.justification: Standard full-vector path patching becomes an explicitly evaluated comparator to the new subspace method across four translation directions, covering component importance, knockout effects, and targeted SFT (v3 Table 9). Appendix F also adds a randomly initialized model comparison. The original Base, Full SFT, and Random SFT comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include top-five knockout/top-32 fine-tuning comparisons, shared versus sentence-specific head ablations, validation on 132 randomly selected samples including errors, and Qwen2.5 pivot analysis. Added evaluations use sentence perplexity, BLEU-1, chrF, TER, and CSI-Match. The original fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained head-count and MLP-count tuning ablations, v3 adds MLP knockout validation, error-inclusive sample robustness, word/sentence shared-head interventions, cross-language head-role analysis, pivot-language investigations, gender/formality and cultural-bias analyses, and qualitative translation-error cases (Appendices E–N). These test substantially broader mechanistic and failure-mode questions.

E5.justification: v3 adds standard-deviation bars for attention distributions, Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests for training-stage comparisons, a Wilson confidence interval and binomial test for head behavior, and a paired t-test for cultural preservation. v1 lacks these statistical reporting practices. Repeated training-run counts and seeds remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Most original fine-tuning scores persist. The appendix En→Zh Targeted SFT entry changes from 27.6/80.0/62.5 (v1 Table 8) to 30.7/81.4/64.3 (v3 Table 14), matching the already-reported main result. Substantial new findings include 46.9% word/sentence head overlap, subspace-versus-standard patching results, and Targeted SFT trailing Full SFT on medical/legal translation (Tables 9, 12, 20).

T1.justification: v3 adds an orthogonal common/specific subspace assumption, a low-rank optimization objective, projection-based intervention equations, and Theorem 1 asserting optimality of the SVD procedure. v1 has no corresponding subspace theory. Appendix C refers the theorem's proof to cited work rather than providing a complete proof locally.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now present a new fine-grained causal intervention method as a central contribution, whereas v1 applies existing path patching. The abstract and conclusion explicitly emphasize generalization from word-identified components to sentence translation. The sparse-head, specialized-role, English-intermediary, and 64-head fine-tuning claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds a training-distribution explanation for pivot-language emergence, including Chinese rather than English in Qwen2.5, and discusses language-dependent head roles. It also interprets specialized-domain performance gaps, gender-related failures, literal translations, noise sensitivity, and hallucinations. These substantially expand applicability boundaries beyond v1's brief limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and data after acceptance; v3 supplies a GitHub code-access link and states that detection and validation datasets are separate. It also supplies additional task-specific counterfactual examples. The disclosed learning rate, batch size, epochs, gradient rescaling, and eight-A100 hardware configuration are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds a related-work discussion of encoder–decoder NMT interpretation and head pruning, positioning the work as the first investigation of decoder-only LLM translation mechanisms. It also grounds the new method in linear-representation, subspace-intervention, and common/specific decomposition research, including Geiger, Makelov, Park, Piratla, and Xie.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, behavioral analysis, and fine-tuning narrative are extensively rewritten. The standalone overview section is removed, detection is reorganized around the new method, and fine-tuning setup/results are consolidated. Appendices are substantially reorganized, with expanded explanations, relocated limitations, and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. v1's overview figure is removed; main translation tables are merged; attention panels and representation plots are reformatted; knockout plots gain MLP series; and attention distributions gain error bars. Numerous new analysis tables and heatmaps accompany retained and relocated figures.

improvement.justification: v1's mechanistic validation largely relies on curated correct word translations and descriptive analyses. v3 substantially strengthens that evidence through direct method comparisons, error-inclusive validation, sentence-level interventions, statistical support, and explicit domain and gender failure analyses. These additions address important weaknesses in validation and applicability. Technical reporting remains imperfect: Algorithm 1 contains dimensional inconsistencies, and sentence-level PPL-change signs conflict between Section 4.2 and Appendix E.2. These problems limit confidence in parts of the revision, but the broader validation and clearer failure boundaries provide a substantial overall gain.
